classification.difficultyReason: The parts scaffold angle calculation and name the triangles to prove similar; then use their corresponding sides and select the appropriate right triangle for Pythagoras.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC with altitude BD to AC; all ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black under house style.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Justify the statement that $\triangle ABC$ is similar to $\triangle ADB$.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle ADB$ by AAA: the angle at $A$ is common and $\angle ABC=\angle ADB=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
In triangles $ABC$ and $ADB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=\angle DAB &&\text{(common angle)}\\\angle ABC&=\angle ADB=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle ADB$ by AAA.

Matching sides of $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle ADB$ give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AC}{AB}&=\frac{AB}{AD}\\\frac{AC}{6}&=\frac{6}{3}\\AC&=12\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

By Pythagoras' theorem in right-angled triangle $ABD$,
$$\begin{align*}BD^2&=AB^2-AD^2\\BD^2&=6^2-3^2\\BD^2&=27\\BD&=3\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

By Pythagoras' theorem in right-angled triangle $ABC$,
$$\begin{align*}BC^2&=AC^2-AB^2\\BC^2&=12^2-6^2\\BC^2&=108\\BC&=6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
